subtopic: Shared memory bank conflicts / Matrix transpose
learningObjective: Analyze a shared-memory transpose kernel and identify which access pattern causes a 32-way bank conflict; know the padding-based mitigation.
stem: Consider the following CUDA matrix-transpose kernel using shared memory, launched with `blockDim = (32, 32)` and `gridDim = (N/32, N/32)` on sm_80. Which statement about shared-memory bank conflicts is correct?

options.text: Both the write (W1) and the transposed read (R1) are conflict-free because sm_80 supports 32-way multicast for shared memory across distinct addresses within the same bank, effectively eliminating serialization.
Write (W1) is conflict-free (row stride-1 across banks); transposed read (R1) causes a 32-way bank conflict since all 32 warp lanes hit one bank; padding to `tile[32][33]` breaks the alignment.
The write (W1) causes a 32-way conflict because 32 threads target the same bank while writing a row; the transposed read (R1) is conflict-free because column accesses spread evenly across banks.

Bank conflicts are automatically eliminated by the CUDA compiler via a promotion pass that pads shared-memory arrays whose access patterns match a canonical conflict template, so no source-level change is required for correctness or performance.

explanation: sm_80 shared memory has 32 banks with 4-byte-wide bank interleaving. In `tile[32][32]`, element `tile[r][c]` maps to bank `c mod 32`. Row write (W1): fix `threadIdx.y`, varying `threadIdx.x` → each thread hits a different bank → conflict-free. Column read (R1): fix `threadIdx.y`, varying `threadIdx.x` on the first index (rows) with fixed column `threadIdx.y` → all 32 threads read column `threadIdx.y`, i.e., addresses `4*(r*32 + threadIdx.y)`; each bank is `addr / 4 mod 32` = `(r*32 + threadIdx.y) mod 32` = `threadIdx.y mod 32` — same bank for all 32 threads → 32-way conflict. Padding to `tile[32][33]` breaks the bank alignment.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: sm_80 supports broadcast (same address across all threads → 1 access) but not multicast for distinct addresses in the same bank.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: the row write is not the conflict; the transposed read is.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: identifies the conflict location and the classic padding fix.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the CUDA compiler does not automatically eliminate SMEM bank conflicts.

assumptions: Default 4-byte shared-memory bank width on sm_80.
The kernel is intended to transpose an N × N matrix with N a multiple of 32.
nonImplications: Does not imply that padded tiles are always faster; padding wastes SMEM capacity, which can lower occupancy.
Does not imply that transpose kernels always need this fix; some architectures or SMEM-swizzle configurations differ.
